description: Five visitor-accessible rounds around St. George: a nationally ranked clifftop at Sand Hollow, Weiskopf's lava-rock finale at Black Desert, the lava-canyon test at Entrada, a Matt Dye daily-fee with a tale of two nines, and a Keith Foster design under Pine Valley Mountain.
intro: St. George might be the best-value desert golf trip in America. You can fly in on a Friday, play a nationally ranked course the same afternoon, and spend the whole trip moving between red rock canyons and black lava fields — never leaving the town's orbit. Southern Utah sits in the 'Color Country' where the Mojave, Colorado Plateau, and Great Basin meet, so every round comes with scenery you will never confuse with anywhere else. Every course below is genuinely open to a traveling golfer, most on an ordinary public tee sheet, and the whole set sits within about 30 minutes of downtown.

sections.heading: 1. Sand Hollow Resort (Championship Course)
paragraphs: The Championship Course at Sand Hollow Resort in nearby Hurricane is the reason golf travelers put St. George on the map. Designed by John Fought with Andy Staples and opened in 2008, the 18-hole par-72 layout stretches past 7,300 yards and has appeared on Golf Digest's 100 Greatest Public ranking, with three of its holes named among America's 100 Greatest Holes. The front nine plays a straightforward desert loop through red rock outcroppings; the back nine climbs a towering ridgeline and traces the edge of jagged cliffs that fall away into a red rock canyon — views so dramatic that golfers reportedly reach for their cameras before their clubs.

Book an early tee time so you can play the ridge holes in good light, and pair it with the resort's 9-hole Links Course — built in a nod to Britain's linksland with hand-built stone 'sheep fencing' — for an affordable, relaxed afternoon round the same day. Sand Hollow suits confident mid-handicaps who want the full desert show; high handicaps can enjoy it from the forward tees, which shrink the carries considerably. Golf Digest calls it a must-play in southern Utah, and for most trips it should be the anchor round. A par-3 Wee Course — southern Utah's only one — makes a fun warm-up or family add-on before tackling the Championship layout.

sections.heading: 2. Black Desert Resort
paragraphs: Black Desert Resort in Ivins is the newest must-play in the state and a legitimate piece of golf history. Opened in 2023, it is the last course Tom Weiskopf was involved in building — his longtime design partner Phil Smith completed the vision after Weiskopf's cancer diagnosis. The public par-72 course plays to 7,500 yards through fields of ancient black lava rock that had to be blasted into golf formations, set against vermilion red rock mountains. It hosted the PGA Tour's Black Desert Championship in October 2024 — Utah's first PGA Tour stop in more than 60 years — followed by an LPGA event in 2025, and it landed on Golfweek's list of the Top 100 Best Courses You Can Play in the U.S.

This is the splurge round of the trip: tee times sell out well in advance, and the experience is fully serviced, with a forecaddie included in every group. Check the tournament calendar before you plan — the course closes to all play for PGA Tour preparations and the event itself in the fall. If you are choosing between the two headline courses, play Sand Hollow for the classic desert red rock and Black Desert for the lava-rock spectacle and the 'I played where the Tour played' memory. Forward tees at roughly 5,400 yards keep the round enjoyable for average players despite the championship length.

sections.heading: 3. Entrada at Snow Canyon
paragraphs: Entrada at Snow Canyon is the most architecturally pedigreed course in the St. George area. Originally designed by Johnny Miller with Fred Bliss in 1996 — the first course in the region routed through the lava fields — it was completely reimagined by David McLay Kidd in a 17-month rebuild that finished in 2022 and won Golf Digest's Best Transformation Award. Set on 710 acres of red sandstone and black lava at the edge of Snow Canyon State Park, the course is famous for its finishing stretch: holes 15, 16, and 17, known as the 'Devil's Cauldron,' play completely surrounded by jet-black lava rock. Kidd's redesign widened those corridors, rebuilt every green in bentgrass, and added more ground-game options.

The catch: Entrada is technically a private club. The visitor's loophole is real, though — guests of the on-site Inn at Entrada get full access to the course, making it one of the better stay-and-play backdoors in destination golf. If you are planning a trip around it, book the room first and arrange the tee time through the pro shop, and expect some of the fastest greens in the region — Greater Zion notes the slope rating ranks among the area's highest. Pair it with a morning hike in Snow Canyon State Park next door; the two sit minutes apart.

sections.heading: 4. The Ledges Golf Club
paragraphs: The Ledges Golf Club is the locals'-favorite daily fee and one of the classic 'tale of two nines' designs in Utah. Open to the public, the 7,200-yard par-72 was designed by Matt Dye — nephew of Pete Dye — and opened in 2006 in a residential community at the foot of the red and white sandstone cliffs of Snow Canyon State Park. The front nine is a tame, linksy loop across wide-open ground with enormous greens; then the back nine turns dramatic, climbing into the foothills with elevation changes, subtle moguls in the fairways, and spectacular views back toward Snow Canyon. A few shorter par 4s are drivable for longer hitters, adding genuine risk-reward decisions.

At roughly 3,600 feet of elevation the ball flies a touch farther than at sea level, so club down on approach shots and don't be surprised when you overshoot a green that looks reachable. Weekday tee times are usually easy to find and pace is fast — play it the morning you arrive as a warm-up for Sand Hollow or Black Desert later in the trip. The practice facilities and Fish Rock Grille make it a comfortable full-morning stop. The dramatic canyon side is the back nine, so save your camera battery.

sections.heading: 5. Coral Canyon
paragraphs: Coral Canyon in Washington, a few minutes east of St. George toward Zion National Park, is the trip's best combination of challenge and value. The public 18-hole par-72, designed by Keith Foster, plays to 7,029 yards across desert washes, 55 bunkers, and two lakes, with the Pine Valley Mountains on the horizon to the north. The course is known as one of the sternest tests on the area's Red Rock Golf Trail: the signature par-3 6th plays across a deep ravine littered with rock outcroppings, while the 488-yard par-4 15th is the course's hardest hole. Kentucky bluegrass fairways and bentgrass greens keep it comfortable underfoot despite the rugged setting.

Position Coral Canyon on a Zion day: play 18 in the morning and you can still reach Zion National Park by afternoon, since the course sits right at the State Road 9 exit toward the park. It's also the most playable-for-everyone pick in this guide outside of The Ledges — multiple tee sets and a straightforward front nine mean shorter hitters can enjoy the scenery without being beaten up. The Grille on site handles lunch, so you don't lose time driving back into town between the round and the park. August aerification week can close the course for maintenance, so check the course calendar before locking in a summer trip.
